content:
Maria PM: quick sync — post-launch metrics are in. main ask: customer A reported a regen failure on the embed hotpath, ~8% of requests failing with 500s. need to decide bug vs enhancement and where it lands in the next sprint.
Sam Eng: can we get a repro + logs? if it's a config edge we'll patch fast. if it's model-related might need a rollback to v1.12.
Alex CSM: customer A flagged this as blocking for a pilot next week. they want ETA.
Rachel QE: reproduced locally with their prompt set — failing when input length > 6k tokens. stack shows OOM in kv-cache resize path.
Jin Design: is this user-visible as degraded UX or hard failure? Alex — what do they see?
Alex CSM: they see truncated responses and repeated 500s. pilot won't proceed unless stable.
Omar SRE: current hosted cluster saw a small uptick in OOM alerts around the same time. not cluster-wide.
Sam Eng: sounds infra + runtime bug. mitigation options: 1) emergency patch to guard against oversized KV allocations, 2) temporary request length cap for affected customers, 3) fallback to an older runtime image that handled KV growth differently.
Maria PM: priority tradeoff: customer A pilot is revenue-informing but we also had planned the conversation-history-quality epic for this sprint. if we pick fix path (1) it's ~2 dev days + QA. (2) is quick but customer impact. (3) is higher-risk rollback. thoughts?
Rachel QE: patch (1) + test vectors from Alex would give highest confidence. I can validate in 1 day with the customer prompt set.
Sam Eng: agree. estimate: 1.5-2 dev days + deploy canary. if we do request cap it's 2-3 hours config change.
Alex CSM: customer prefers no visible cap for pilot. they'd accept short maintenance window.
Jin Design: flag: some clients will notice the maintenance banner. we should craft copy: "brief stability update — back in ~30m".
Maria PM: decision: ship emergency patch (1) in this sprint, move convo-quality epic to next iteration. we need launch criteria for the patch: <1% error rate on canary, no regressions on latency (>+20ms).
Sam Eng: noted. I'll open a PR and tag @Rachel QE and @Omar SRE for canary monitoring.
deploy-bot: scheduled canary deploy for runtime-patch-1739 at 2026-03-22T09:00Z — /deploy canary to proceed.
Omar SRE: canary watchers: latency, 5xx rate, GPU memory tail. alert if 5xx > 1% for 10m.
Rachel QE: I'll run customer A prompt set against canary once up. test script: ```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d @prompts.json https://api.redwood.ai/generate
```
Sam Eng: creating a short rollback playbook in PR description — steps to flip to v1.12 if canary breaches thresholds.
Maria PM: communication plan: Alex to tell customer A we have a targeted patch and a planned canary tomorrow AM, with expected window. mention maintenance but avoid long-term cap talk.
Alex CSM: will send them a CTA and offer to run their tests during canary.
Jin Design: I'll queue a short maintenance banner and a follow-up note template for status updates.
Maria PM: backlog reprioritization: moving convo-quality epic to next sprint, keep critical perf tasks that unblock other customers. adding a new bug ticket: "kv-cache-resize oom on long inputs" with severity P1.
Sam Eng: ok. will link PR to that ticket. we should also add a guard in request validation to avoid silent OOM callers in future.
Rachel QE: after canary + customer validation, schedule a hotfix release and a quick regression sweep.
Omar SRE: post-mortem? let's capture root cause and a mitigation timeline. not full Stop-the-World but us writing short RCA to share with CS.
Maria PM: agreed. owners: Sam for fix, Rachel for tests, Omar for canary monitoring, Alex for customer comms, Jin for UX copy. I'll update roadmap docs and move convo-quality to next sprint.
Alex CSM: thanks — I'll loop the customer and set expectations.
Sam Eng: PR open: https://git.redwood/internal/pull/3821 — tagging reviewers.
Maria PM: great work team. post-launch lesson: prioritize quick safety patches that protect pilots over higher-scope quality improvements when customer commitments are at stake. :thumbsup:
